messages:
maya: Heads-up — proposing a short-lived analyst entitlement workflow for SIEM streams. Need input on tokenized export vs proxy view.
ashok: +1. Can you outline the threat model? who gets unwrap ability?
luca: For incident triage, analysts need a 1h window to query raw traces; want minimal unwrap ops. Prefer ephemeral tokenized exports (single-use).
maya: Threat model: external vendor analysts + internal Tier2. Proposal: tokenized stream with per-request KMS unwrap via proxy; tokens expire after 60m. Audit trail includes CMK operation id and requester identity.
security-bot: New policy draft uploaded: https://redwood.internal/policies/temp-entitlement-draft (latest version v0.3)
ashok: Questions: who can request tokens? self-service via ticket? automation? need to avoid manual bottleneck during incidents.
maya: Flow sketch: 1) analyst opens ticket (incident-id + justification) 2) approval by incident owner or security oncall 3) system mints short-lived export token scoped to dataset + single-use nonce + TTL 4) proxy enforces de-tokenization only for that token and logs CMK unwrap details.
luca: How do we ensure tokens can't be replayed after export? Recommend binding nonce to CMK unwrap operation and marking nonce used atomically in DB before unwrap.
maya: Implementation note (prototype API):
```
POST /siem/exports
{ "dataset": "auth-traces", "scope": "incident:1234", "ttl": 3600, "nonce": "uuid-v4" }
Authorization: Bearer <requester-svc-token>
```
Proxy validates ticket, mints signed token -> stores nonce -> allows exactly one CMK-unlock event for that nonce.
ashok: Audit requirements: must capture ticket id, approver, unwrap time, cmk_key_id, proxy_instance_id, and requester identity. For retention: recommend audit logs retained 2 years; raw exported snapshots retained 90 days by default (longer by exec exception).
maya: Security controls: require MFA + higher approval for TTL > 24h. Also add automatic rollback if downstream consumer reports unexpected data.
oncall-mike: Oncall ops note: add emergency bypass procedure (manual key escrow) — require 2-person signoff (security + incident owner) and explicit ticket entry, with automatic alerts to leadership.
luca: Cross-tenant/multi-org exports: block raw unwrap for external vendors. Instead allow tokenized anonymized aggregates or synthetic sets. Internal cross-tenant requires exec OK and must be scoped tight.
maya: Risk checklist: unauthorized CMK usage, token replay, stale approvals, broker compromise. Mitigations: single-use nonce, per-request CMK audit event, short TTL, RBAC for approvers, HSM-backed CMKs only accessible via proxy.
ashok: Action items: - I'll draft RBAC roles for token requester / approver / auditor. - luca to prototype single-use nonce/atomic-mark flow in proxy. - oncall-mike to add emergency key-escrow playbook steps. - maya to update policy doc and include sample ticket template.
maya: Sample ticket template for requests:
```
Title: SIEM Export Request — INCIDENT-1234
Requester: <name>
Scope: auth-traces 2026-03-20..2026-03-21
Justification: Triage for incident 1234 - PII excluded unless approver allows full unwrap
Requested TTL: 3600s
Approver: <incident-owner>
```
ashok: ack, I'll have a first pass RBAC draft by EOD tomorrow.
luca: I'll push a minimal proxy change to ensure nonce is set and checked before unwrap. Expect PR by midweek.
maya: Thanks all — I'll add the emergency-escape flow and finalize v0.3. :thumbsup:
